usage: This is the standard morning greeting used every day by all Moroccans. It is appropriate in both formal and casual settings, typically used from dawn until around noon. The phrase does not change based on the gender or number of people being addressed.

variants.label: standard reply
variants.note: This is the most common reply when someone says sba7 lkhir to you.

variants.label: affectionate
variants.note: Used with close friends, family, or romantic partners to sound warmer.

variants.label: wishing a good day
variants.note: Used to wish someone a blessed or successful morning, often said when parting ways early in the day.

examples.english: Good morning, how are you doing? (to a man)
Good morning, did you all sleep well?

examples.arabic: صباح الخير، بغيت قهوة كحلة عفاك.
examples.english: Good morning, I would like a black coffee please.
